title: Local henselian ind-etale algebras are integral over the base henselization
statement: Let $f:A\to D$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, with $D$ henselian local [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and ind-etale over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Put $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)$. Here $A^h_{\mathfrak p}$ means the henselization of $A_{\mathfrak p}$: the henselian local ring with its universal local map from $A_{\mathfrak p}$ (initial among local maps from $A_{\mathfrak p}$ to henselian local rings). The map $f$ factors through the canonical local homomorphism $A^h_{\mathfrak p}\to D$, and $D$ is integral over $A^h_{\mathfrak p}$: every element of $D$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A^h_{\mathfrak p}$. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Sentence between Theorems 6.3 and 6.4, printed p. 13: local henselian ind-etale algebras are integral over a base henselization; the prime is the contraction of the maximal ideal. Ordinary henselization: algebra.tex Tags 04GN and 04GQ.

proof.text: Put $H=A^h_{\mathfrak p}$ and let $\eta:A\to H$ be the structural map. The contraction $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)$ is prime. If $s\notin\mathfrak p$, then $f(s)\notin\mathfrak m_D$, so $f(s)$ is a unit in the local ring $D$. Thus the formula $a/s\mapsto f(a)f(s)^{-1}$ gives the unique map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to D$ extending $f$, and its inverse image of $\mathfrak m_D$ is $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$. It is a local map. By the initial property of the henselization specified in the statement, this local map extends uniquely to a local homomorphism $h:H\to D$. In particular $h\eta=f$ and $h^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)=\mathfrak m_H$.

source.place: Tags 00CO and 07BH (fractions and local rings); henselization universal local-map convention in the item, compatible with Tags 04GN and 04GQ. This step applies that defining universal property.

proof.text: Choose a small filtered presentation $D\cong\varinjlim_i E_i$ by etale $A$-algebras with coprojections $u_i:E_i\to D$, as supplied by the definition of ind-etale. Fix an arbitrary $d\in D$. The element-representative assertion for filtered colimits of commutative algebras gives an index $i$ and $e\in E_i$ such that $u_i(e)=d$. The presentation is a colimit in commutative $A$-algebras, exactly the category to which that assertion applies; no injectivity of the maps $u_i$ or of the transition maps is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit), ring/algebra elementwise model; Categories Tag 04AX for a filtered indexing category. Expansion of the sentence between Huebner--Schmidt Theorems 6.3 and 6.4.

proof.text: Set $C=H\otimes_A E_i$. The formula $g(x\otimes y)=h(x)u_i(y)$ defines an $H$-algebra map $g:C\to D$, since $h\eta=f$. In particular $g(1\otimes e)=d$. Etale base change, applied to $A\to E_i$ and $\eta:A\to H$, shows that $H\to C$ is etale. The etale quasi-finiteness theorem therefore says both that $C$ is a finitely generated $H$-algebra and that $H\to C$ is quasi-finite at every prime of $C$.

source.place: Tag 00U2 (lemma-etale), base-change clause (3) in the local source; Tag 00U5 (lemma-etale-quasi-finite).

proof.text: Apply the henselian finite-type product decomposition to the henselian local ring $H$ and its finite-type algebra $C$. It gives an $H$-algebra isomorphism $C\cong F_1\times\cdots\times F_n\times B$, where each $F_j$ is local and finite as an $H$-module, and $H\to B$ is not quasi-finite at any prime over $\mathfrak m_H$. Here $n=0$ and $B=0$ are allowed. Retain $g$ as a map out of this product via the displayed isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04GJ (lemma-mop-up), applied with R=H and S=C.

proof.text: Write $e_1,\ldots,e_n,e_B$ for the coordinate idempotents of this finite product, which are pairwise orthogonal and sum to $1$. Every idempotent $a$ of a local ring is $0$ or $1$: one of $a,1-a$ is a unit, and $a(1-a)=0$. Consequently exactly one of $g(e_1),\ldots,g(e_n),g(e_B)$ is $1$ and all the others are $0$. Indeed their sum is $1$ and orthogonality excludes two values equal to $1$ in the nonzero local ring $D$. If $e_*$ is the selected idempotent, then $g(z)=g(e_*z)$ for every $z\in C$. Thus $g$ factors as the projection to the selected factor followed by an $H$-algebra map from that factor to $D$.

source.place: Tag 04GJ product decomposition, elementary coordinate-idempotent argument for a map to a local ring.

proof.text: The selected factor cannot be $B$. Otherwise write $g=v\circ\operatorname{pr}_B$ and put $\mathfrak q=v^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)$. This is a prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak m_H$ because $v$ extends the local map $h$. Let $k=H/\mathfrak m_H$ and $\mathfrak Q=g^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)$. In the fibre over $\mathfrak m_H$, the primes belonging to the $B$ factor form the basic open $D(e_B)$: localizing the product at $e_B$ kills every other factor and gives $B\otimes_H k$. Under this identification the fibre primes associated with $\mathfrak Q$ and $\mathfrak q$ agree. Quasi-finiteness of $H\to C$ at $\mathfrak Q$ says that this point is isolated in the full fibre spectrum. Restrict its open singleton to $D(e_B)$; it remains an open singleton in $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_H k)$. By the definition of quasi-finite at a prime, $H\to B$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$, contradicting step 4. The finite-type hypothesis here holds because the product projection $C\to B$ is surjective, so the images of generators of $C$ generate $B$.

source.place: Tag 00PL (definition-quasi-finite), isolated-point-of-fibre definition; Tag 04GJ residual-factor condition. The fibre identification is the explicit localization at the coordinate idempotent.

proof.text: Hence the selected factor is some $F_j$, with $g=v\circ\operatorname{pr}_j$. Let $e_j$ now denote the image of $1\otimes e$ in $F_j$. Since $F_j$ is a finite $H$-module, the finite-algebra integrality theorem provides a monic polynomial $P(T)=T^r+\sum_{a<r}c_aT^a\in H[T]$ such that $P(e_j)=0$. Apply the $H$-algebra map $v:F_j\to D$ to this equality. As $v(e_j)=d$, the resulting equality is $d^r+\sum_{a<r}h(c_a)d^a=0$. Thus $d$ is integral over $H$ via the canonical local map $h$. Since $d$ was arbitrary, $D$ is integral over $A^h_{\mathfrak p}$, as required.

source.place: Tag 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral); elementary application of the H-algebra map to the monic equation.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q16-28cf732ad (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 7 steps in full, plus the statement of every cited node. I checked the Stacks places (algebra.tex 04GJ lemma-mop-up l.42418, 00U5 l.39456, 00U2, 00GK, 00PL, 00D6, 04GN l.42971 and 04GQ l.43125) and Hübner–Schmidt p.13 from the public PDF. That paper is not under literature/ and is WANTED in the report. Its sentence reads: 'If A→B is ind-étale with B local, henselian, then B is an integral A^h_p-algebra for some prime ideal p ⊂ A.' The item states exactly this, with p = f^{-1}(m_D) and the canonical local map made explicit. It uses ordinary henselization, defined inline by the initial local-map property, which agrees with 04GN/04GQ. Nothing is weakened and no hypothesis is added. Steps: (1) local A_p→D, then the universal property gives h; (2) a representative d = u_i(e) from the elementwise filtered-colimit node; (3) étale base change to H⊗_A E_i, then 00U5 gives finite type and quasi-finite; (4) 04GJ decomposition over the henselian H; (5) the local ring D selects one coordinate idempotent; (6) the B factor is excluded because Spec(B⊗k) = D(e_B) is clopen in the fibre, so quasi-finiteness at Q gives quasi-finiteness at q, against step 4; (7) a finite factor is integral (00GK), and the monic equation is pushed through v. All hypotheses hold where they are used. Small cases tested: fields, Z_(p)^h, Z_(p)^sh, Q over Z. There are no new nodes. The grep found no duplicate, and the parent and lem-trf-artin-join-theorem-6-3 use the conclusion in exactly this form. I accept both declared tool_uses (00U5 and 04GJ ring-theory nodes) as generic black boxes. No SGA source is used. This is not a target node, so no base-change or coefficient comparison applies. No fixes were made. review.md written.

lean.statement: theorem indEtale_local_henselian_integral (A D : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing D] (f : A →+* D) [HenselianLocalRing D] (hind : f.IndEtale) (p : Ideal A) (hp : p = Ideal.comap f (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal D)) [p.IsPrime] (H : Type u) [CommRing H] [Algebra (Localization.AtPrime p) H] [HenselianLocalRing H] (hH : Algebra.IsHenselizationAtPrime A p H) : ∃! h : H →+* D, IsLocalHom h ∧ h.comp ((algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime p) H).comp (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime p))) = f ∧ RingHom.IsIntegral h
